## Ontario Freelance Design Contract Checklist

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/file-earmark-text.svg

Use this checklist before signing a $4,500 logo and brand identity agreement. It focuses on payment protection, revision scope, and ownership timing so you can stay professional and avoid scope creep.

## Contract Review Points, Risks, and Negotiation Position

| Area | What to confirm | Common risk | Firm position |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scope of work | Exact deliverables: logo files, brand guide, color palette, typography, usage examples | “Brand identity” can expand into extra assets with no added fee | Define deliverables in writing and list what is excluded |
| Deposit | 50% upfront deposit and when it becomes non-refundable | Starting work without cleared deposit | Do not begin until deposit is received |
| Revision rounds | Exactly 2 revision rounds and what counts as a revision | Unlimited feedback loops disguised as “small changes” | State that extra rounds are billed separately |
| Ownership transfer | Rights transfer only after final payment | Client uses drafts before paying in full | Keep copyright with you until payment clears |
| Source files | Whether working/source files are included, and when | Immediate release of editable files before payment | Release source files only after final payment, if included at all |
| Timeline | Milestones, review deadlines, and client response times | Delays caused by slow feedback with no schedule protection | Add client response deadlines and project pause language |
| Usage rights | What the client can use immediately vs after payment | Client assumes they own all files from day one | Grant limited review/use rights until final payment |
| Kill fee / cancellation | What happens if the project ends early | Losing time and not getting paid for completed work | Include payment for completed stages and cancellation terms |
| File formats | Final export formats versus editable working files | Delivering more than agreed, for free | Separate final deliverables from source assets |
| Change requests | How new directions are handled | Major strategy changes treated as “revisions” | New concepts or direction changes = additional scope |

## Professional but Firm Negotiation Approach

- Acknowledge the client’s request without arguing: “I understand why you want flexibility and quick access.”
- Reframe the policy as standard practice: “My contract protects both sides by tying ownership and source files to final payment.”
- Offer a compromise, not a concession:
  - Two revision rounds are included.
  - Additional rounds can be quoted hourly or as a flat add-on.
  - Final exported files can be delivered before source files, if needed.
- Keep wording calm and businesslike:
  - “I’m happy to be flexible within the agreed scope.”
  - “Unlimited revisions would make the project open-ended, so I work with defined rounds.”
  - “Editable source files are released once the project is fully paid.”
- Avoid apologizing for standard terms. State them as your process, not a debate.

## Client-Friendly Script You Can Use

Subject: Contract terms for the logo and brand identity project

Hi [Client Name],

I’m excited to move forward on the logo and brand identity project. I reviewed the contract and wanted to confirm a few standard terms so we’re aligned before signing.

The project includes:
- 50% deposit to begin work
- 2 revision rounds
- Final ownership and source file transfer after the final payment is received

I’m not able to offer unlimited revisions or release editable source files immediately, but I’m happy to include the agreed revision rounds and provide final export files during the project. If you need additional revisions or extra file formats, I can quote those separately.

These terms help keep the timeline clear and protect both of us from scope creep. If that works for you, I’m ready to sign and get started.

Best,
[Your Name]
